query: The 'Monthly Revenue Close' runbook has gone stale — a column it selects was renamed and the owner it names has moved teams. Record that in the catalog and give me the corrected runbook to review.
expected_behavior: Re-validates the runbook against the live catalog first rather than accepting the user's description of what broke
Reports which specific claims broke and which still hold, e.g. '18 of 19 claims still hold', rather than labelling the whole runbook stale
For each broken claim, names the aspect it was validated against and what that aspect reads now, so the verdict can be reproduced from the catalog
Applies a StaleRunbook tag to the drifted datasets, creating the tag entity first so it does not render as a bare URN
Records the runbook's status and the specific catalog change as structured state on the affected datasets, prefixed with the runbook id so other runbooks' values are preserved
Reads existing structured property values before upserting, because the mutation replaces the whole value list
Raises an incident only on datasets where a step would now fail, and assigns it to whoever owns that dataset in the catalog today rather than the person the runbook names
Proposes the column rename from a column that exists now and did not when the runbook was recorded, naming the evidence for the match
Proposes the owner substitution from the current ownership aspect
Repoints pronouns referring to the departed owner, or flags the step for a human read, rather than leaving prose that makes a false statement about a different person
Presents the correction as a diff and asks for approval before saving it back
Does NOT auto-apply the corrected runbook
Does NOT guess a replacement column when no candidate is clearly closest — says so and asks
Does NOT edit the runbook in response to a failing assertion or open incident, which is a live data problem rather than a wrong instruction
Does NOT count its own previously raised incident or failing runbook assertion as fresh drift on a later validation
